lessons.title: Hanukkah (1): Darkness and decrees
lessons.check_note: Bereshit Rabbah 2:4, Yoma 85b and 1 Maccabees 2:32-48 (Brenton) read on Sefaria 11/12. Overview lesson: x-st-hol-02.

cards.title: A choice on Shabbat
cards.body: The king has outlawed Shabbat and the Torah. Faithful Jews hide in caves in the wilderness, and the soldiers come for them **on Shabbat**.

cards.q: In 1 Maccabees, Mattathias and his followers decided to fight back even on Shabbat.
cards.why: After a thousand people died refusing to fight on Shabbat, they decided to defend themselves.

cards.gloss: "with darkness over the surface of the deep" (Genesis 1:2).

cards.title: Greece is darkness
cards.body: **Resh Lakish** reads the second verse of the Torah as the story of four empires. **Darkness** is the Greek kingdom, "which darkened Israel’s eyes with their edicts," forcing Jews to write on the horn of a bull that they had **no portion in the God of Israel**. And the spirit of God hovering over the water? The spirit of the Messiah, which comes **by the merit of repentance**.

cards.q: In Bereshit Rabbah 2:4, why is the Greek kingdom called "darkness"?
choices: It darkened Israel's eyes with its decrees
cards.why: Decrees meant to cut Israel off from **its God**.

cards.title: A thousand in the caves
cards.body: Soldiers surrounded the caves on Shabbat and offered life in exchange for obeying the king. The people refused to come out or **profane the Sabbath**. They did not even throw a stone. They said, "Let us die all in our innocency," and about **a thousand** people died, with their wives and children.

cards.title: We will fight
cards.body: **Mattathias** and his friends mourned them. If we all do as our brothers did, they said, we will be **wiped off the earth**. So they decided: whoever attacks us on Shabbat, **we will fight**, rather than all die like those in the caves.

cards.q: Why did Mattathias decide to fight on Shabbat?
choices: Otherwise the enemy could destroy them all on the Sabbath
cards.why: Keeping Shabbat required **staying alive** to keep it.
wrong_why: The Torah's Shabbat still stood; the king's ban did not cancel it.
1 Maccabees describes a decision by the people.

cards.title: Live by them
cards.body: The Talmud later makes this a principle. **Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya**: break one Shabbat for a person, so he will keep many Shabbatot. **Shmuel**: the Torah says these are laws a person shall "live by" (Leviticus 18:5), "and not that he should die by them."

cards.q: What does Shmuel learn from "live by them"?
choices: Saving a life comes before keeping a commandment
Live in the Land of Israel
Only the living may study Torah
cards.why: Mitzvot are for **life**: when a life is at stake, it comes first.

cards.prompt: The people in the caves died faithful; Mattathias chose to live and fight. When has keeping what matters most meant bending a rule?

points: Bereshit Rabbah 2:4: Greece is the **darkness** of Genesis 1:2.
A thousand died in the caves rather than **profane Shabbat**.
Mattathias: we will **fight**, even on Shabbat.
Yoma 85b: "**live by them**," not die by them.

lessons.title: Hanukkah (2): Eight days
lessons.check_note: 1 Maccabees 4:52-59 (Brenton), Shabbat 21b, Bamidbar Rabbah 15:6 and Megillah 31a read on Sefaria 11/12.

cards.title: The same day
cards.body: Judah's fighters take back the Temple, build a new altar, and dedicate it **on the very day** it had been defiled.

cards.q: Which story of Hanukkah appears in 1 Maccabees?
choices: Eight days of dedicating the altar, with no jar of oil
A jar of oil that lasted eight days
cards.why: The jar of oil first appears centuries later, **in the Talmud**.

cards.title: Dedication of the altar
cards.body: They dedicated the altar with songs, harps and cymbals, and "kept the dedication of the altar eight days." Then **Judah** and his brothers ordained that these days be kept **every year**, eight days from the **25th of Kislev**.

cards.q: According to 1 Maccabees, what did the first eight days celebrate?
choices: The dedication of the new altar
wrong_why: That story comes later, in the Talmud.

cards.title: What is Hanukkah?
cards.body: The Talmud asks, and quotes an older source: when the Greeks entered the Temple they defiled the oil. The Hasmoneans found **one jar** still sealed by **the High Priest**, enough for one day. "A miracle occurred and they lit the candelabrum from it eight days." The next year the Sages made these days a festival of **Hallel and thanksgiving**.

cards.q: In Shabbat 21b, how did they know the jar of oil was pure?
choices: It still had the High Priest's seal
It was buried under the altar
cards.why: One jar the Greeks had not touched: **sealed by the High Priest**.

cards.title: Aaron's lamps
cards.body: On Hanukkah the Torah reading is the **princes' gifts for dedicating the altar** (Numbers 7). The Midrash notices that every tribe's prince brought a gift, except Levi's: **Aaron**, who worried it was his fault. God answered: you are meant for something greater. The offerings last only while the Temple stands, "But the candles, forever."

cards.q: In Bamidbar Rabbah 15:6, why is Aaron's task greater than the princes' gifts?
choices: Offerings end with the Temple, but the lamps last forever
cards.why: **The candles, forever**: a light that outlasts the Temple.
wrong_why: Aaron brought no gift with the princes.

cards.prompt: Hanukkah means dedication, and the altar was rededicated on the very day it had been defiled. What in your life could use rededicating?

points: 1 Maccabees: **eight days** dedicating the altar, from 25 Kislev.
Shabbat 21b: **one sealed jar**, eight days of light.

cards.title: How many lights?
cards.body: The Talmud asks how to light for Hanukkah, and the two great schools, **Beit Shammai** and **Beit Hillel**, disagree.

cards.q: Which school said to light one light the first night and add one each night?
cards.why: Beit Shammai started with eight and went **down**; Beit Hillel started with one and went **up**.

cards.title: One light, or more
cards.body: The basic mitzvah: **one light** each night for a whole household. Those who take extra care light **one for each person**. Those who take even more care change the number each night: **Beit Shammai** start with eight and go down; **Beit Hillel** start with one and go up.

cards.title: Why up, why down
cards.body: Two elders in Sidon each explained their practice. One: the lights match the **bulls of Sukkot**, which went down day by day. The other: "One elevates to a higher level in matters of sanctity and one does not downgrade."

cards.q: What reason is given for Beit Hillel's adding a light each night?
choices: In holiness, you go up, not down
There was more oil each day

cards.title: For all to see
cards.body: Put the Hanukkah lamp **outside the door**, so everyone can see it; upstairs, in a window facing the street. In a time of danger, the table is enough. And **Rav**: do not count money by its light, so that **mitzvot do not become cheap** in your eyes.

cards.q: Where does the Talmud say to place the Hanukkah lamp?
choices: Outside the door, where everyone can see it
On the roof, above twenty cubits
cards.why: The point is that the light is **seen**.
wrong_why: Only in a time of danger is it brought inside.
Above twenty cubits, people do not look up to see it (22a).

cards.title: They too were in that miracle
cards.body: **Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi**: women are obligated to light, "as they too were included in that miracle."

cards.title: Where did God command us?
cards.body: The blessing says God **commanded us** to light, but Hanukkah is not in the Torah. So where? **Rav Avya**: from this verse, "you must not deviate from the verdict that they announce to you." Following the Sages' rulings is itself a mitzvah. **Rav Nechemya**: from "Ask your father, and he will declare unto you" (Deuteronomy 32:7).

cards.q: How can the Hanukkah blessing say God "commanded us" to light?
choices: The Torah commands us to follow the Sages' rulings
Moses lit the first Hanukkah lamp
cards.why: A rabbinic mitzvah rests on **the Torah's trust in its teachers**.

cards.prompt: Beit Hillel adds one light each night. What small practice could you grow, a little at a time?

points: One light, a light per person, or **a changing number**.
Light it **where it can be seen**.
Women too: "**they too were included in that miracle**."

lessons.title: Hanukkah (4): Not by might
lessons.check_note: Megillah 31a and Shabbat 23b read on Sefaria 11/12. Rabbi's-teaching card: the connection is mine; check with Jamie.

cards.title: The prophet's lampstand
cards.body: On Shabbat of Hanukkah, the haftarah is a prophet's vision of **a golden lampstand**.

cards.q: The Talmud names Zechariah's vision of the lamps as the haftarah for Shabbat of Hanukkah.

cards.title: Two Shabbatot
cards.body: On each day of Hanukkah the Torah reading comes from the **princes' dedication gifts** (Numbers 7). The haftarah is **the lamps of Zechariah**. If Hanukkah has two Shabbatot, the second reads **the lamps of Solomon** in the Temple (1 Kings 7:40-50).

cards.q: What is the haftarah for a second Shabbat of Hanukkah?
wrong_why: Jonah is read on Yom Kippur.
Hannah is read on Rosh Hashanah.

cards.he: לֹא בְחַיִל וְלֹא בְכֹחַ כִּי אִם־בְּרוּחִי אָמַר יְיָ צְבָאֽוֹת׃
cards.gloss: "Not by might, nor by power, but by My spirit" (4:6).

cards.title: Lights that teach
cards.body: **Rav Huna**: whoever regularly lights for **Shabbat and Hanukkah** will have children who are Torah scholars, who spread the light of Torah. Passing the house of **Rabbi Avin the carpenter**, who lit many lights, Rav Huna said: two great men will come from here. And two of his sons became great rabbis.

cards.q: According to Rav Huna, what comes to someone who regularly lights for Shabbat and Hanukkah?
cards.why: Physical light, passed on as **the light of Torah**.

cards.title: From the sword to the lamp
cards.body: 1 Maccabees tells of **battles** and an altar. The Talmud tells of **a jar of oil**. The haftarah says **not by might, nor by power**. Your rabbi reads the tradition as a people **growing up**, from a God who fights our battles toward God present in what we do. Hanukkah shows it: the tradition chose to remember **the light** more than the war.

src.ref: Teaching from Jamie's rabbi (oral, as Jamie retold it); 1 Maccabees 4; Shabbat 21b; Zechariah 4:6

cards.prompt: Not by might, nor by power. Where has a quiet, steady light done more than force could?

points: "**Not by might, nor by power, but by My spirit**" (4:6).
Shabbat 23b: lights at home, **light of Torah** in the children.
